metadata.status: Context-informed subjective elicitation; numeric anchors are assumptions, not measured or externally validated district rates.
metadata.time_invariance: One distribution per district and parameter for the entire target period. Seasonal and recurrent disruption mechanisms inform typical process variation, not year-specific parameter shifts.
metadata.outcome_separation: No malnutrition prevalence, outcome ranking, acute-malnutrition phase or outcome-derived treatment-need estimate was used in elicitation. Outcome-bearing search material and an unexpectedly mislinked Hiran IPC document were discarded; the latter was excluded in its entirety.

parameterization.conversion: a = mean * concentration; b = (1 - mean) * concentration

units.p: monthly exit probability by any modeled exit route
units.gamma: monthly new entries divided by district under-5 population
units.omega: total standard deviation of monthly entries divided by district under-5 population

parameterization.strength_interpretation: Concentrations implement the requested informative subjective priors. They are analyst choices, not sample sizes or evidence-based effective sample sizes. Limited evidence reduces concentration without mechanically increasing any mean.
parameterization.independence: Only marginal priors are specified. A joint prior, population-dependent arrival distribution and dependence between parameters are not identified by these hyperparameters.

elicitation_assumptions.absolute_scale: Context supports relative comparisons but does not identify absolute p, gamma or omega. Monthly gamma anchors 0.007-0.020 and omega anchors 0.003-0.012 were selected directly on their required scales; none was back-calculated from a prevalence target.
elicitation_assumptions.p: Monthly p anchors 0.20-0.36 assume that improved treatment/referral access increases net exit and that constrained delivery tends to prolong untreated episodes. These imply 1/mean(p) durations of approximately 2.8-5.0 months, not posterior duration estimates; E[1/p] differs from 1/E[p].
elicitation_assumptions.mortality_and_persistence: District-specific fatality hazards, spontaneous recovery and untreated duration were not verified. No district is asserted to have a known acute-fatal or persistent disease phenotype, and no mortality-driven p uplift was imposed. The access-to-p relationship is a conditional assumption because mortality could counteract it.
elicitation_assumptions.gamma: Livelihood concentration, asset poverty, restricted food access and established displacement hosting influence relative incidence assumptions. Urban service and trade opportunities can buffer vulnerability without eliminating it.
elicitation_assumptions.omega: Means encode physical-process mechanisms: seasonal food and milk access, floods and drought, population movements, insecure trade and price changes. They do not encode measurement error, missing data or confidence in the elicitation.
elicitation_assumptions.district_aggregation: Districts combine urban, rural and displaced populations. Livelihood assignments are qualitative mixtures; verified district under-5 population weights were unavailable. No claim of population-weighted zone averaging is made.
elicitation_assumptions.service_access: Higher p in towns is an inference from settlement concentration, referral opportunities and access context. It does not claim measured CMAM coverage, proven treatment success, or uninterrupted supplies in any district.
elicitation_assumptions.food_insecurity_baseline: A verified typical district IPC Acute Food Insecurity phase over 2017-2021 was not established. No district phase was invented or used to calibrate a numeric rate.
elicitation_assumptions.displacement: Major hosting adjustments are limited to documented centres and the Mogadishu-Afgooye corridor as a geographic inference; the existence of a displacement assessment alone was not treated as evidence of a large displaced share.
elicitation_assumptions.validation_limit: High informativeness is conditional on the stated scenario anchors. Context alone cannot justify precise epidemiological calibration; sensitivity to the absolute means and concentrations remains material.
